newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutor says accused army rapist used rank to prey.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor says accused army rapist used rank to prey.

text.p: Army prosecutors at the court-martial of a sergeant accused of raping six women said in opening statements Friday the drill instructor used the power of his position to prey on female trainees sexually.

"This case is about rape. It's about power, access, and control," prosecutor Capt. David Thomas said at the outset of the trial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, focal point of the military's biggest sex scandal since the Navy was rocked by the 1991 Tailhook affair.

Simpson's attorneys said their client had engaged only in consensual sex. "A number of female soldiers in training were attracted to and willingly engaged in sexual intercourse with Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson," defence attorney Capt. Edward Brady said in his opening statement.

Brady said Army investigators used excessive zeal in interviewing witnesses. "Their own witnesses will tell you that (investigators) actively encouraged them to embellish their statements ... to 'make it jucier,'" he said.

Simpson, 32, faces 19 counts of rape and 39 other charges including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment involving 13 women. He has pleaded innocent to the charges but earlier pleaded guilty to 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five counts of propositioning.

The alleged acts occurred in 1995 and 1996, while Simpson was a drill instructor at the Ordnance Centre and School at the Aberdeen Proving Ground, overseeing classes of five to 45 soldiers receiving advanced instruction after basic training.
Simpson's was the highest-profile case and the first trial in a probe of sexual misconduct by trainers at the base.

An 11th soldier, Sgt. 1st Class Tony Cross, was charged Friday with sodomy, adultery and failing to obey an order in a case involving four women. Four of the cases have been resolved through plea bargains or administrative proceedings. There have been no rape convictions.
"This is the rape case that they (the Army) must win," Simpson attorney Frank Spinner told reporters after the first day's court session. "Simpson is basically their showcase."

Thomas said in his opening statement that Simpson used a commanding physical presence and authority over female soldiers to force and intimidate them into having sex. He asked Simpson, who wore an Army dress uniform and sported a shaved head as he sat with his attorneys, to stand and display the full impact of his 6-foot, 4-inch height.
"The accused had a system," Thomas said. He said Simpson determined which trainees would be vulnerable, then exploited any weaknesses he could.

Thomas said Simpson ordered one woman to masturbate in his office, then raped her. Another, whose Army career he had rescued by intervening with higher-ups, was raped twice after being told "you owe me." A third woman was raped eight times. Others he threatened to kill if they told on him, Thomas said.
"This was not consensual sex," he said. "There wasn't any romance here. It was: Take your clothes off, lie down on the floor ... stop crying, and after the sex put your clothes on and leave."

The first prosecution witness, Warrant Officer Paul Wiatr, was a senior drill sergeant overseeing Simpson. He called Simpson a self-described "company asshole" who was proud of being "mean" but who nonetheless inspired strong loyalty among his trainees and drew high performance from them.
Wiatr said he had heard of no complaints about Simpson while Wiatr was stationed at the ordnance centre.
Simpson's alleged victims are scheduled to begin testimony Monday.

The investigation at Aberdeen prompted a nationwide military probe into sexual harassment after it was disclosed in November. It has led to criticism that the military failed to prevent the sexual harassment as well as to charges that investigators unfairly targeted black soldiers and tried to coerce rape accusations from witnesses.
Deciding the case, which is expected to last two to three weeks, will be a six-member military jury composed of one white woman, two black men and three white men. Four of the jurors are officers.

Simpson faces a maximum penalty of life in prison if convicted of rape. On the guilty pleas, he faces a total maximum penalty of 32 years in jail, a dishonourable discharge and forfeiture of pay and allowances.
